discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 0b6e96f80b. `factsOf` now reads only the messages after the newest real prompt (a user message whose `userRunSpan` isn't 0), so an earlier turn's edits or errors no longer drive Verify, Review or Fix; reminders, hook context and steering that core injects mid-run carry `userRunSpan: 0` and stay inside the turn.

Declining this one. No code path produces an image-shaped object inside tool arguments or tool schemas, so this is a theoretical under-count. If it ever occurred, the budget scaling from the provider's actual input count (compaction.ts, `underestimateFactor`) and overflow recovery already bound the damage. Scoping the replacer per path isn't worth the complexity.

vLLM's `/v1/models` reports the window as `max_model_len` (it's on its ModelCard), so a vLLM source still falls back to 128K even though the comment at the top lists vLLM. Worth adding `entry.max_model_len` here?

On LM Studio's `/api/v0/models`, `max_context_length` is the model's ceiling, and a loaded model also reports `loaded_context_length`, which is what it actually serves (can be a lot smaller). Since maxInputTokens falls back to contextWindow and that's the compaction budget, compaction won't kick in before LM Studio starts rejecting. Prefer `loaded_context_length` when it's present?

```suggestion
			workspaceName: basename(cwd),
			rules: CLOUD_SESSION_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
			mode,
			providerId: "cline",
			platform: "Linux",
		});
```

-// Converse request. They pin the reason for the adapter floor of 5.0.65:
-// OpenAI models reached through inference profiles (`us.openai.*`,
-// `global.openai.*`) must get `reasoning.effort`, the field Bedrock accepts,
-// not the generic `reasoningConfig` that older adapters emitted for any id
-// they did not recognise (cline/cline#14451, vercel/ai#19403).
+// Converse request. Together they pin the adapter floor:
+//
+//   1. OpenAI models reached through inference profiles (`us.openai.*`,
+//      `global.openai.*`) get `reasoning.effort`, the field Bedrock accepts,
+//      not the generic `reasoningConfig` that adapters before 5.0.65 emitted
+//      for any id they did not recognise (cline/cline#14451, vercel/ai#19403);
+//   2. models the adapter cannot classify get no reasoning fields at all,
+//      instead of a `reasoningConfig` Bedrock rejects for models without
+//      reasoning support — adapters before 5.0.96 sent it for every
+//      non-Anthropic id (cline/cline#14095, vercel/ai#21487);
+//   3. the families the adapter does classify keep their native shapes from
+//      the id alone even when the catalog does not list the model, so a
+//      catalog that lags a model launch never switches thinking off.
+//
+// Cases that would only assert the adapter's translation for an id it
+// classifies belong to the adapter's own suite and are deliberately absent.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Intentional. That case exercised none of Cline's routing; it only pinned how `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` translates an id it classifies itself, which belongs to the adapter's own suite. The remaining cases pin what goes through Cline's resolver, catalog lookup and portable-reasoning path, and the live run in the PR body records Nova 2 Lite's accepted request shape.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
The 32k floor is intentional following review feedback: applying 30% directly lowered existing output allowances and could cause more truncation and retries.
Compared with main, an 8k model still receives an 8k cap, and a 64k model still receives 32k. Only sufficiently large models receive an increase. For example, 128k → 38,400. The existing model and context clamps remain in place.
The PR description still described the earlier proportional reduction; I’ve corrected it. Using the fraction directly would reintroduce the issue identified in the earlier review, so I believe this P1 can be closed.

This guard avoids inserting context into an unresolved tool-call/result pair, but deferral does not guarantee delivery. If the next response contains no tool calls, the run can finish without reaching the post-tool flush; the next run clears pendingHookContexts. The new "defers run-start context past a seeded trailing tool call" test actually asserts that resume-context is absent, so it covers dropping the context rather than eventual delivery. Could we either resolve/validate incomplete seeded history before the first request and then inject the context, or explicitly reject this unsupported history shape? Please test the selected behavior instead of silently losing context. This is a narrow resume edge case, not a claim that the normal run-start path is broken; simply removing the pairing guard would not be a safe fix.
good catch, deferral could drop it.  now it goes in right before the trailing tool call, so it always lands and the pair stays adjacent
